endorsements.quote: Form a multidisciplinary AI governance committee. Explicitly include nursing leaders, physicians, data scientists, IT professionals, compliance professionals, and patient/family representatives.
Form a multidisciplinary AI governance committee.

Establish metrics: (1) discrimination + calibration, (2) subgroup performance (race/ethnicity, language, sex, age, payer, SDOH), (3) workload & safety (alert burden, overrides, near-misses, reported harms), (4) drift (data/performance checks with escalation thresholds).

AI literacy should progress across 3 levels: (1) foundational—understanding key AI concepts and ethical issues; (2) applied—interpreting model outputs and integrating them into clinical decisions; and (3) leadership—governing and evaluating AI tools.

Operationalizing nursing participation in AI governance will require structural and resource support—such as protected time for nurse leaders to serve on governance committees, funding for AI literacy and competency training, and data access mechanisms that enable nurses to review model inputs and outputs.
Develop targeted AI literacy programs (AI basics, bias detection, and interpreting outputs).

Establish metrics: (1) discrimination + calibration, (2) subgroup performance (race/ethnicity, language, sex, age, payer, SDOH), (3) workload & safety (alert burden, overrides, near-misses, reported harms), (4) drift (data/performance checks with escalation thresholds).
Use a charter, model registry, risk levels, and stage-gates (design → testing → implementation → monitoring).
Additionally, health systems can lay a stronger foundation for responsible AI by requiring transparency from AI vendors about model training, validation, and limitations.

unlisted_practices: Explicitly include nurses in AI governance, design, development, and performance monitoring, with protected time and dedicated informatics roles.
Involve nurses in problem definition, vendor evaluation, and tool design, including workflow mapping, pilot testing with bedside teams, and human factors reviews.
Integrate AI ethics, governance, and data literacy competencies into pre-licensure, graduate, and continuing nursing education.
Apply the BE FAIR framework to position nurses as equity stewards in bias identification and mitigation across the AI lifecycle.
Create dashboards of model performance metrics for real-time decision-making and use findings for updates, retraining, and governance adjustments.
Include pharmacists, social workers, case managers, and patient and family representatives in AI governance.
